hints: Look at the functional group in the middle of the formula, this waxy solid is an ester, not a carboxylic acid or alcohol.
Split the molecule at the $\text{CO}_2$ link: the $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{CO}$ part comes from the acid and the $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}$ part comes from the alcohol.
Remember alkaline hydrolysis with aqueous NaOH gives a sodium carboxylate from the acid side and a neutral alcohol from the alkyl side, so match each chain to its correct product type.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the ester**

This is a classic ester hydrolysis question in disguise. The $\text{CO}_2$ in the middle is shorthand for the ester link $\text{COO}$.

$$\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{CO}_2\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33} \text{ is } \text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{COO}\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}$$

**Recall alkaline hydrolysis**

Heating an ester under reflux with aqueous NaOH causes saponification. The ester bond breaks to give a carboxylate salt plus an alcohol, not two salts.

$$\text{RCOOR' + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{Na + R'OH}$$

**Assign each chain correctly**

The acyl side $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{CO}$ becomes the sodium salt $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$. The alkoxy side $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}$ becomes the neutral alcohol $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}\text{OH}$.

$$\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{CO}_2\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{CO}_2\text{Na + C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}\text{OH}$$

options.A: Incorrect because the two chains are swapped round. The $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}$ chain is attached to $\text{C=O}$, so it must form the carboxylate, not an $\text{ONa}$ species, and the $\text{C}_{16}$ chain cannot form $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$.
options.B: Incorrect because $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}\text{ONa}$ is a sodium alkoxide. In aqueous NaOH the alcohol product is protonated by water to give the neutral alcohol $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}\text{OH}$, not the alkoxide.
options.C: Incorrect because the products are reversed. $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}$ is the acid-derived side so it forms $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$, not $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{OH}$, and $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}$ is the alcohol-derived side.
options.D: Correct. Alkaline hydrolysis cleaves the ester to give sodium palmitate, $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{31}\text{CO}_2\text{Na}$, from the carboxylic acid part and cetyl alcohol, $\text{C}_{16}\text{H}_{33}\text{OH}$, from the alkyl part.
